messages:
jess: Heads-up — reproducible latency spike on moe-100b when KV prefix cache + dynamic batching are enabled. All tokens pile into the all-to-all stage and p99 jumps. profile attached but pasting highlights here.

omar: Can you share a flame/timeline? Is this only with expert_parallel=true or across variants?

jess: Only when expert_parallel=true and tensor_par=2, pipeline_par=4. Timeline shows a big stall in alltoallv (~200–600ms/step). Minimal nvprof extract: ```alltoallv 0.43s 
memcpy H2D 0.12s 
ncclAllToAll 0.38s 
kernel matmul 0.05s```

linh: Sounds like fanout skew + many tiny messages. Are we sending per-token routing vectors instead of packed routing batches?

sam: I instrumented the batcher — our heuristic currently emits routing packages per-request when kv_cache_hit toggles the effective seq_len. With large prefix cache hits, seq_len drops but expert_fanout per token rises -> lots of small alltoalls.

jess: Exactly. Cache warm path reduces compute per-token but increases routing chatter (short messages, more messages).

kai: Two quick mitigations to try: 1) bucket tokens by target-expert and locally aggregate small messages before alltoall, 2) switch NCCL algorithm to ring for small-message workloads. Also try overlapping comm/compute with separate CUDA streams + events.

profiler-bot: FYI metrics snapshot: expert_fanout_99p=18, alltoall_calls_per_sec=1250, avg_alltoall_msg_size=5KB, nvlink_util=0.82

omar: We tried bucketing in a prototype but hit memory blowup from per-expert temp buffers on GPU. Could we cap per-expert buffer size and spill to replicated experts or fall back to single-expert routing when capped?

linh: Also note kernel-selection regression: after the last compiler pass the fused MLP kernel is slower for short sequences (<64). For seq_len<64 fallback to baseline matmul+gelu reduced end-to-end latency in microbenchmarks (lower launch overhead).

sam: Proposed canary plan: enable route-bucket-aggregation with buffer_cap=4096 tokens + spill_to_replicas=true, and set seq_short_kernel_threshold=64 to force fallback kernel. Canary run: 2 hours on a small fleet.

jess: Test runner command I used: ```python tools/run_moe_canary.py --model=moe-100b --duration=7200 --config=configs/canary_bucket.json```

kai: Also add telemetry hooks: per-batch alltoall_msg_count, avg_msg_size, nccl_algo_in_use, per-expert-buffer-utilization. If we can correlate p99 tail with msg_count and avg_msg_size that validates the mitigation.

omar: Roll strategy: if canary passes, roll to 20% traffic. Watch memory pressure; if per-gpu mem spikes revert aggregation. Also check cost delta (more memcpy vs less kernel time).

sam: One more optimization: our KV warm path does a host->device memcpy for the whole prefix before routing, which duplicates data movement. Reorder: local KV lookup + compute routes -> alltoall of only small routing indices -> remote KV fetch. That should reduce H2D duplication and lower alltoall blocking.

jess: Nice. I'll open a PR with the bucket agg + kernel fallback + KV reorder experiments and attach perf flames once CI runs.

kai: :thumbsup: tagging infra to give a small fleet for the canary and add NCCL logging.

profiler-bot: Added dashboard panels: moe_routing_msg_count, moe_alltoall_latency, kv_memcpy_bytes. Will stream alerts if p99 > 300ms.

jess: Thanks all — will follow up with PR link and flame graphs. :eyes:
